summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with T1-T2 paraplegia and chronic COPD on baseline oxygen, was admitted for hypoxia and productive cough. She was found to have pneumonia and a urinary tract infection caused by multidrug-resistant Klebsiella. She was initially treated with vancomycin and cefepime, then switched to vancomycin and piperacillin-tazobactam due to antibiotic resistance concerns. She received prednisone for COPD exacerbation and nebulizers for bronchodilation. Her fever resolved, oxygen needs decreased, and she was discharged home on a 14-day course of IV antibiotics with home nursing support. She returned to baseline mental status and was able to resume her regular medications with adjustments for anxiety and pain.
